draft.title: Charges in electric fields
card: Two parallel plates with a potential difference V across them, set a distance d apart, make a uniform electric field between them. Its strength is E = V/d.
A charge q in this field feels a force F = qE. The force is the same at every point between the plates. It points along the field for a positive charge and against it for a negative charge.

A charge that enters at right angles to the field keeps a constant velocity along the plates, because there is no force in that direction. Across the plates it has constant acceleration a = F/m, as in projectile motion.
The path is a parabola while the charge is between the plates. Once it leaves the plates, there is no force and it moves in a straight line.
draft.remember: Between plates the force is constant, so a charge follows a parabola like a projectile.

a.q: A proton enters the space between two charged parallel plates, moving parallel to them. What is the path of the proton between the plates?
opts: A parabola, curving towards the negative plate
A circle, centred between the plates
A straight line, parallel to the plates
A parabola, curving towards the positive plate
a.why: The field gives a constant force across the plates, while there is no force along them. Constant acceleration in one direction with constant velocity in the other gives a parabola. A proton is positive, so it curves towards the negative plate. A circle would need a force that always changes direction.
a.clue: Think of a ball thrown sideways under gravity.

b.q: Two plates 0.040 m apart have a potential difference of 200 V across them. An electron (charge 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) is between them. What is the size of the force on it?
b.why: E = V/d = 200 ÷ 0.040 = 5000 V/m. F = qE = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ × 5000 = 8.0 × 10⁻¹⁶ N. Using V in place of E gives 3.2 × 10⁻¹⁷ N, which skips the step of dividing by the distance.
b.clue: Find the field strength first, then the force.

a.best: A parabola, curving towards the negative plate
